Erebor, Lonely MountainThe Hobbit: The Battle of the Five ArmiesFive armies. One table.Every recipe serves 4.
    StartersMainsSweetsDrinks
    StartersLake-town smoked fishRye crispbread with crème fraîche, smoked trout, dill and pickled onionHow to make it200g smoked trout1 packet rye crispbread200ml crème fraîche1 bunch dill1 jar pickled onionsSlice a few pickled onions into thin rings and pick the dill into small sprigs.Spread each rye crispbread with crème fraîche.Flake the smoked trout over the top and finish with a dill sprig and a few onion rings.Arrange on a wooden board and serve cold.Dáin's Iron Hills meat piesMuffin tin pies of beef and onion gravy under puff pastryHow to make it500g beef mince1 brown onion250ml beef stock2 sheets of shortcrust pastry2 sheets of puff pastry1 tbsp vegetable oil1 bottle tomato sauceDice the onion and cut the pastry into rounds to fit a 12-hole muffin tin.Brown the mince and onion in oil, add the stock and simmer until thick.Cool the filling for 15 minutes while you line the tin with shortcrust rounds.Fill each case, top with a puff pastry lid and cut a small steam hole.Bake at 200°C until golden, then serve with tomato sauce.Dale campfire damper with golden syrupThe survivors camping in the ruins of DaleHow to make itAs written, serves 4Damper of self-raising flour, butter and milk, baked at 200°C for 30 minutes, torn and served with butter and golden syrup.Rub 60g cold butter into 450g self-raising flour and a pinch of salt.Stir in 300ml milk to make a soft dough and knead lightly.Shape into a round, sit on a lined tray, cut a deep cross on top and dust with flour.Bake at 200°C for 30 minutes until it sounds hollow when tapped.Tear into chunks while hot and serve with soft butter and a jug of golden syrup.MainsErebor roast beef and Yorkshire puddingsRoast beef sirloin with Yorkshire puddings baked in a muffin tinHow to make it1.5kg beef sirloin140g plain flour4 eggs200ml full cream milk300ml beef stock2 tbsp vegetable oilsalt and pepper, to tasteTake the beef out of the fridge, season well and make the batter by whisking flour, eggs and milk. Rest the batter while the beef cooks.Roast the beef at 220°C.Drop to 180°C and keep roasting.Rest the beef under foil, then heat oil in a muffin tin at 230°C.Pour the batter into the hot tin and bake until puffed and golden.Make gravy from the pan juices and stock, then carve the beef.Elvish lemon and herb roast chickenThranduil's elves arriving at the mountainHow to make itAs written, serves 4Chicken roasted with lemon, garlic and herbs, with roasted root vegetables and a herb salad.Mix 50g soft butter with lemon zest, 2 crushed garlic cloves and chopped parsley, thyme and tarragon.Push it under the skin of a 1.8kg chicken and put the zested lemon inside.Toss 1kg parsnips, carrots and beetroot in chunks with oil and salt.Roast the chicken on top of the veg at 200°C for 75 minutes.Rest 10 minutes.Dress rocket and herbs with lemon juice and oil and serve with the carved chicken and veg.SweetsBag End auction day crumbleGreen apple and blackberries under an oat crumbleHow to make it4 green apples250g blackberries100g brown sugar100g butter100g rolled oats100g plain flour500ml custardPeel and slice the apples.Cook the apples with the blackberries and some of the sugar until just soft, then spoon into a dish.Rub the cold butter into the oats, flour and remaining sugar and scatter over the fruit.Bake at 180°C until golden and bubbling.Warm the custard and serve over the crumble.DrinksBag End hot spiced apple juiceWarm apple juice with cinnamon, cloves, star anise and orange peelHow to make it1 L cloudy apple juice4 cinnamon sticks5 whole cloves2 star anises1 orange1 tbsp brown sugarPeel three strips of zest from the orange and slice the rest of it thinly.Simmer the apple juice with the cinnamon, cloves, star anise, zest and sugar over low heat, without boiling hard.Strain into mugs and add a fresh cinnamon stick and an orange slice to each.
